literal: Even in the world of gods and here in this world, to obtain other good things than benevolence is rare.
translation: Both in the world of the gods and in this earthly world, it is difficult to find any other good thing that is better than benevolence.
modern: தேவர் உலகத்திலும் இந்த உலகத்திலும் ஒப்புரவை விட (பிறருக்கு உதவி செய்வதை விட) சிறந்த வேறு நன்மைகளைப் பெறுவது அரிது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of benevolence (oppuravu), which means living in harmony with society and doing one's duty to others. The poet compares this virtue across two realms: the celestial world of the gods (puttēḷ ulakam) and this earthly world (īṇṭu). It asserts that in neither of these worlds can one acquire any good quality or possession that is superior to benevolence. Thus, serving and sharing with society is established as the highest possible good a person can attain.
